transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… it’s like my body isn’t really listening to me anymore. At first I was pacing around my apartment all night, making all these notes for a supper-club idea I had—like menus, seating, lighting, all of it, and I don’t even know why I thought I had to do it right then. But lately it’s the opposite. I’m so slowed down that my sister says it takes me forever just to get my shoes on. That’s kind of what scared me enough to come in.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?

I don’t think so… I mean, not like seeing someone standing there who isn’t there or hearing a voice talking to me, no. Sometimes at work it’s loud and I think someone called my name, but that happens to everyone, right? The kitchen bell, people yelling “corner,” plates clattering—so I don’t know if that counts, but I haven’t noticed anything weird like that.
Have you had a strong belief that you had special powers, a special mission, or abilities that other people said weren’t real?

Yeah… I mean, I didn’t think of it as “special powers,” exactly. But I was completely convinced I was going to build the best bilingual supper club in the city, like it was obvious and everyone else was just behind. I kept thinking investors would be stupid not to back me.

Which is kind of ridiculous saying it now, because I didn’t even have the money lined up, and I wasn’t working at the time. But in my head it felt… certain. Like I’d figured out something everyone else was missing.
During the time you were making all those plans, did you feel unusually high, euphoric, or on top of the world?

Yeah… kind of. After I got fired, which was a whole thing—my manager acted like I’d personally ruined the restaurant or something—I felt weirdly unstoppable. Like excited, wired, like this was actually the start of something better.

But then if anyone questioned it, like my sister saying maybe I should slow down or someone asking how I’d pay for it, I’d just… snap. I’d get so mad, like they were trying to ruin my life or take this huge chance away from me.
Have you had a period of at least several days when you felt persistently very down or depressed?

Yeah… not just several days. It’s been more like, I don’t know, about three months now where everything feels heavy and slowed down.

Like, I’ll sit there and mean to get up, and then it’s an hour later. It’s weird because I used to be the person rushing around a restaurant with five tables yelling for things, and now even basic stuff feels like walking through wet cement. Three months sounds dramatic, but… yeah, around that long.
During these past three months of feeling slowed down and depressed, have you had any beliefs that other people said weren’t true?

I don’t think so… I mean, not like before, where I was sure I had this big thing figured out and everyone else just couldn’t see it.

These past months it’s more been like… I don’t know, everything feels flat and pointless, but that’s not really a “belief” other people are arguing with me about. My sister will say I’m being too hard on myself, but that’s different, right? Like when she tells me I’m not as useless as I think, I don’t know if that counts or if that’s just… her trying to be nice.

Sorry, I’m kind of circling. I don’t think I’ve had any beliefs that people said weren’t true.
During that wired, unstoppable period, did you need much less sleep than usual?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I remember being really caught up in everything, like I’d start doing one thing and then suddenly I was looking up something totally different, like menus or names or whatever, and then I’d get annoyed because people kept interrupting me.

Sleep-wise… I don’t know if I was sleeping less or if it just felt like the days were all kind of running together. I wasn’t really keeping track. My apartment was a mess then too, which probably doesn’t answer your question. I guess I didn’t really notice needing less sleep in a clear way.
During that wired, unstoppable period, were you hospitalized for your mental state?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. Like, do you mean hospitalized overnight, or just taken somewhere to be checked out?

I wasn’t really… I don’t know, I’m trying to remember it clearly, but that whole stretch is kind of jumbled in my head. I remember people being really worried, and I remember a lot of arguing, but the actual “was I hospitalized” part—I don’t want to say yes or no if I’m mixing things up.

Sorry, I know that’s probably not helpful.
During that wired, unstoppable period, were you unable to keep working or take care of your usual responsibilities because of your mental state?

Yeah… I mean, yes, I think that’s the part people were most upset about. I wasn’t keeping work straight at all—like shifts, plans, who I’d promised what to—and then rent stuff got all tangled too. I kept thinking I was about to fix it, like if I just reorganized everything, but I’d end up with piles of notes and no actual thing done.

And my family kept calling because I’d said I’d do things and then I just… didn’t. Or I’d start something else. My sister finally had to take me to the crisis clinic because I couldn’t get the basic stuff organized on my own. Like normal responsibilities were just not happening.
About how long did that wired, unstoppable period last?

I think… about four months? It started after I got fired from the restaurant, which is weird because at first I kept telling myself it was just stress, like anybody would be thrown off by that.

But yeah, if I’m actually lining it up, it’s been going on for around four months. I kept meaning to get back on track, and then more time would pass.
During that wired, unstoppable period, did you ever believe something that other people said was definitely not true?

Yeah… I guess so. I mean, at the time it didn’t feel false, it felt obvious. I really believed I was about to build the best bilingual supper club in the city, like this whole restaurant-nightlife thing, and that investors would be idiots not to back me.

Which sounds ridiculous now because I didn’t even have a job then, or money lined up, but I was talking like it was basically guaranteed. I had menus and names and this whole… I don’t know, concept. I kept telling people they just didn’t understand the vision.
